correctness.rationale: The claimed orbit partition is correct over C, conditional on the directly checked published fact that the 72 type-9 points are the 9-torsion points other than 3-torsion. The Hessian of the Fermat cubic is proportional to xyz; any plane automorphism preserves its triangle, is monomial and has group (mu_3)^2 semidirect S3, order 54. All type-9 coordinates are nonzero and the order-9 diagonal subgroup acts freely. The stabilizer of [x:y:z] corresponds exactly to the S3 projective stabilizer of [x^3:y^3:z^3]. The source polynomial q(t) satisfies q(1)=-243, excluding any transposition; only [1:omega:omega^2] and [1:omega^2:omega] are fixed by a 3-cycle. Each cube triple has 9 projective lifts, giving one 18-point orbit with stabilizer C3 and a complementary free 54-point orbit. On F the condition of two primitive-root cube ratios is equivalent to x^6+x^3y^3+y^6=0 and x^9=y^9=z^9.
residual_risks: Uses published standard Gattazzo/Merta–Zięba identification of type-9 points with the 72 non-3 9-torsion points; result confined to this smooth plane Fermat cubic over characteristic zero.

originality.rationale: The full primary Artebani–Dolgachev 2008/2009 Hesse-pencil study supplies a stronger equivalent geometric decomposition. Its Proposition 5.2 constructs eight Halphen cubics B_1,...,B_8, each intersecting any smooth Hesse pencil member in a nine-point E[3]-translation orbit, and their union is the 72 non-3 9-torsion points. Its displayed generators act on the indices by B_i->B_{i+4} and a pair of 3-cycles fixing indices 1 and 5; therefore on the Fermat member they give exactly the index orbits {1,5} and {2,3,4,6,7,8}, i.e. 18 and 54 points. The same paper identifies an invariant sextic Phi_6 meeting the Fermat cubic in the 18 exceptional points from B1 and B5. Reducing its formula on F yields 12(x^6+x^3y^3+y^6); similarly B1 B5 yields 3 times that sextic. Thus ALL distinctive components of the proposed result are mathematically implied by a published antecedent, irrespective of absence of identical 18+54 wording. That decisive primary comparison overrides negative keyword searches and the older self-review PASS.

value.rationale: The type-9 point symmetry question is a natural geometric invariant in principle, and a genuinely unknown full orbit/stabilizer classification could be scientifically valuable even if narrow. This instance is not an unknown exact invariant: Artebani–Dolgachev already provide the eight nine-point Halphen orbits, exact projective action on them, the special two-cubic/18-point subsystem, and the corresponding sextic invariant. Translating their explicit 2+6 orbit table into 18+54 and using orbit–stabilizer, then simplifying their invariant sextic on F, is an immediate specialization/computation rather than a new substantive mathematical result. The package adds neither new structure, proof method, boundary, nor independent unknown classification surviving antecedent coverage.
residual_risks: A fuller historical survey could find still older equivalent classical geometry, but that would not reverse the already decisive 2008 coverage.
